text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Cabinet to ignore parliamentary rejection of decision to allow limited night flights at Beek Airport near Maastricht. (p1)
- KLM shares rise eight percent on news of possible sale of part of 38 pct state interest in airline. (p1)
- Bed manufacturer Beter Bed to be floated on Amsterdam Stock Exchange, priced between Dfl 25-28, on Dec. 5. (p1)
- Shipyard Van der Giessen-De Noord forecasts loss this year. (p3)
- South Korean-appointed consultancy Bain & Co. gives positive advice on bankrupt plane maker Fokker. (p3)
- Retailer SHV Makro starts experiment with home-shopping via TV-set in cooperation with KPN subsidiary MultiMall. (p3)
- Technical wholesaler Econosto finalises takeover of Van der Beyl Beheer of Rotterdam. (p3)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer buys New Zealand's publisher Adis International. (p5)
- Builder Dura seeks to improve profit margin. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- ABN AMRO's U.S. takeover target Standard Federal says Ohio-based savings bank Charter One offered $47 million more after Standard Federal board accepted ABN bid. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Falling interest rates and strong Wall Street pushes Amsterdam Stock Exchange to new record at 623.27. (p1)
- Liberals want cheaper purple-coloured diesel for truckers to keep costs for transport sector low. (p7)
- KLM's Cargo to transfer European road cargo to Jan de Rijk Logistics of Roosendaal. (p25)
- Transport and storage group Pakhoed to issue 16 million limited convertible depositary receipts at Dfl 12.50 per share. (p27)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) extends bid for Australia's TNT until Dec. 12. (p27)
- Dredging division of Ballast Nedam receives orders worth Dfl 200 million. (p31)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Royal Dutch/Shell chief Cor Herkstroeter denies company preparing bid for British Gas. (p11)
- Philips Electronics closes Roermond plant and Unilever shuts snacks plant in Veldhoven. (p11)
